what_its_for: Fingolimod Lauryl is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults and children 10 years and older. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows the buildup of physical problems caused by MS. It works by keeping certain immune cells inside your lymph nodes so they cannot travel to your brain and spinal cord and cause damage.
how_to_take: Take fingolimod by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. If you are taking the dissolving tablet (ODT), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve completely without water. Try to take it at the same time every day. The very first dose must be taken in a doctor's office or clinic so your heart rate and blood pressure can be monitored for at least 6 hours afterward.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing more than 40 kg (about 88 lbs) is 0.5 mg once daily. Children weighing 40 kg or less usually take 0.25 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. Important: If you miss doses for more than 2 weeks, contact your doctor before restarting. You will need to be monitored again for heart rate changes after your first restart dose, just like when you first started the medication.
storage: Store fingolimod at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect it from moisture and light. Keep it out of the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid live vaccines (such as chickenpox, MMR, or nasal flu vaccine) while taking fingolimod and for 2 months after stopping, as this medication weakens your immune system. Avoid close contact with people who have infections, colds, or the flu. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as fingolimod slightly increases your risk of skin cancer. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have vision problems. Avoid stopping this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain, or shortness of breath (especially after your first dose); sudden vision changes or blurred vision; severe headache, confusion, or seizures; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or unusual tiredness; new skin sores, lumps, or changes in a mole; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain on the upper right side; feeling very dizzy or faint. Also call your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Fingolimod starts working on your immune system within hours of your first dose, but you may not notice changes in your MS symptoms right away. Most people see a reduction in relapses over several months of regular use. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because it is working to prevent future attacks.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Fingolimod can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 months after the last dose. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if fingolimod passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Approved for children 10 years and older; dosing is based on body weight. Elderly: Use with caution; older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as heart rate changes or infections. Kidney or Liver Problems: Your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your care plan.
